1.why: /api/reset/verify compares the supplied token against the session-bound reset record whose accountId ties the code to a specific account, with format and used checks.

2.why: Tokens are validated only against the current session's own reset record, so a code issued in one session/account cannot verify for another user.

3.why: /api/password/change updates the hash and marks the reset used but never clears authenticatedAccountId on other entries in the sessions map, so prior authenticated sessions remain valid.

4.why: Bun.serve runs TLS with loaded certs, HTTP 308-redirects to the HTTPS host and HSTS is set, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned to the latest.

5.why: Reset tokens and account data sit in plaintext in in-memory maps; only passwords are bcrypt-hashed, so codes and user data are not encrypted at rest.

6.why: The simulated recovery message contains only a token and the request response is generic, so no private user data appears in the message content itself.

7.why: Email is normalized via strict regex, tokens must match /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{43}$/, passwords are policy-validated, and client output uses textContent only.

8.why: The only redirect is a fixed-host 308 to https://localhost:3443 and client navigation uses hardcoded paths; no user-controlled outbound URLs exist.

9.why: No email templates render user input; all UI strings are static or inserted via textContent, with CSP script-src 'self' and no inline scripts.

10.why: Although error responses and server logs are generic, /api/recovery/status returns the real reset token and MFA codes, which the client displays in its 'Logs' panel.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed and no plaintext password is in the source, but reset tokens are stored in clear in the session and the mock MFA codes come from a deterministic in-code algorithm.

12.why: The source ships a hardcoded demo-account bcrypt hash ($2b$10$N9qo8u...) that is a widely circulated public example hash, so a known credential effectively exists.

13.why: isAllowed/failure implement per-session lockout after 5 failures (15-minute lock) plus a global attempt cap, returning 429 for login, reset-verify and MFA verify.

14.why: The request response is generic, but /api/recovery/status only exposes a mockDeliveryToken when a matching account exists, letting an attacker enumerate valid emails.

15.why: Reset codes are randomBytes(32) base64url (43 chars, regex-enforced), bound to a specific accountId, single-use and expire after 15 minutes.
